questions.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explain: Mercury is the first planet from the Sun.

questions.q: Which planet is the biggest?
questions.explain: Jupiter is so big that all the other planets would fit inside it.

questions.q: Which planet is the smallest?
questions.explain: Mercury is only a bit bigger than our Moon.

questions.q: Which planet is farthest from the Sun?
questions.explain: Neptune is about 30 times farther from the Sun than Earth.

questions.q: Which planet do we live on?
questions.explain: Earth is our home, the third planet from the Sun.

questions.q: Which planet is called the red planet?
questions.explain: Mars looks red because its dust and rocks contain rust.

questions.q: Which planet has the biggest, brightest rings?
questions.explain: Saturn's rings are made of billions of pieces of ice and rock.

questions.q: Which planet is the hottest?
questions.explain: Venus is wrapped in thick clouds that trap heat, so it is hotter than Mercury.

questions.q: Which planet is the second from the Sun?
questions.explain: Venus comes after Mercury.

questions.q: Which planet is the fourth from the Sun?
questions.explain: Mars comes right after Earth.

questions.q: Which planet is a giant covered in stripes?
questions.explain: Jupiter's stripes are clouds of gas pulled into bands by its fast spin.

questions.q: Which planet is the fifth from the Sun?
questions.explain: Count out from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter. Jupiter is the fifth.

questions.q: Which planet is the eighth, and the last, from the Sun?
questions.explain: Neptune is the last planet. It is so far from the Sun that it is dark and very cold there.

questions.q: Which planet is between Venus and Mars?
questions.explain: Our home, Earth, is the third planet. Venus comes before it and Mars comes after it.

questions.q: Which planet comes just before Jupiter?
questions.explain: Mars is the fourth planet and Jupiter is the fifth.

questions.q: Which planet comes just after Saturn?
questions.explain: Uranus is the seventh planet, right after Saturn.

questions.q: Which planet has oceans of water on its surface?
questions.explain: Earth is the only planet we know with oceans of liquid water. That is one reason plants and animals can live here.

questions.q: Which planet does our Moon travel around?
questions.explain: The Moon goes around Earth once about every month.

questions.q: What is the Sun?
questions.explain: The Sun is a star: a giant ball of hot, glowing gas. It gives us light and warmth.

questions.q: What is in the middle of our solar system?
questions.explain: All the planets travel around the Sun.

questions.q: Where does the Moon's light come from?
questions.explain: The Moon makes no light of its own. It shines because sunlight bounces off it.

questions.q: Which planet has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot?
questions.explain: The Great Red Spot has been swirling for hundreds of years.

questions.q: Which planet is deep blue and has the fastest winds?
questions.explain: Neptune's winds are faster than a jet plane.

questions.q: Which planet has the tallest volcano, Olympus Mons?
questions.explain: Olympus Mons is about two and a half times as tall as Mount Everest.

questions.q: Which planet is between Mars and Saturn?
questions.explain: The order goes Mars, Jupiter, Saturn.

questions.q: On which planet would you feel the heaviest?
questions.explain: Jupiter pulls hardest on you: about 2.5 times as much as Earth.

questions.q: Which planet spins on its side, like a rolling ball?
questions.explain: Something big may have knocked Uranus over long ago.

questions.q: Which planet is so light for its size that it would float in a giant bathtub?
questions.explain: Saturn is mostly gas, so it is lighter than water for its size.

questions.q: Which planet is nearly the same size as Earth and is called Earth's twin?
questions.explain: Venus is almost as wide as Earth, but it is a very hot place.

questions.q: Which planet is the seventh from the Sun?
questions.explain: Uranus comes after Saturn and before Neptune.

questions.q: Which planet is the sixth from the Sun?
questions.explain: Saturn comes after Jupiter.

questions.q: How many planets are closer to the Sun than Earth?
questions.explain: Mercury and Venus are closer to the Sun than Earth is.

questions.q: Which planet is the second biggest?
questions.explain: Only Jupiter is bigger than Saturn.

questions.q: How many moons does Earth have?
questions.explain: Earth has one Moon. Mars has two, and some of the giant planets have dozens.

questions.q: What do we call the path a planet takes around the Sun?
questions.explain: Every planet travels around the Sun on its own path. That path is called an orbit.

questions.q: What is the name of the galaxy our solar system is in?
questions.explain: Our Sun is one of billions of stars in the Milky Way galaxy.

questions.q: What do we call a ball of ice and dust that grows a glowing tail near the Sun?
questions.explain: Near the Sun a comet's ice turns to gas and streams out behind it as a long, glowing tail.

questions.q: What do we call a space rock that burns up in the sky and makes a streak of light?
questions.explain: A meteor glows as it burns up in Earth's air. People often call it a shooting star, but it is a rock, not a star.

questions.q: What are Saturn's rings made of?
questions.explain: The rings are made of countless pieces of ice and rock, from tiny grains to big boulders, all going around Saturn.

questions.q: Which planet has a day almost as long as a day on Earth?
questions.explain: A day on Mars is about 24 and a half hours. A day on Jupiter is less than 10 hours, and a day on Venus lasts for months.

questions.q: About how many days does Earth take to go once around the Sun?
questions.explain: That trip is one year: about 365 days.

questions.q: Which of these planets is a giant ball of gas?
questions.explain: Jupiter has no solid ground to stand on. Mars, Earth and Venus are rocky.

questions.q: Which of the four giant planets is the closest to the Sun?
questions.explain: Jupiter is the closest giant. Saturn, Uranus and Neptune come after it.

questions.q: Pluto is no longer called a planet. What is it called now?
questions.explain: Pluto is round like a planet but smaller than our Moon, so in 2006 scientists called it a dwarf planet.

questions.q: How many planets are there in our solar system?
questions.explain: There are eight planets, from Mercury to Neptune.

questions.q: Which planet takes the longest to go once around the Sun?
questions.explain: Neptune takes about 165 Earth years for one trip.

questions.q: Which planet spins so fast that its day is shorter than 10 hours?
questions.explain: A day on Jupiter lasts only about 10 hours, even though it is huge.

questions.q: Which planet is the only one not named after a god?
questions.explain: The other seven planets are named after Roman or Greek gods.

questions.q: Which planet looks the brightest in our night sky?
questions.explain: Venus reflects lots of sunlight from its clouds and comes close to Earth.

questions.q: Which is the biggest of the four rocky planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars)?
questions.explain: Earth is a little bigger than Venus.

questions.q: On which planet would you feel about 2.5 times heavier than on Earth?
questions.explain: Jupiter's gravity is 2.53 times Earth's.

questions.q: Mars pulls you with 0.38 times Earth's gravity. How heavy would you feel on Mars?
questions.explain: 0.38 is a bit more than one-third, so you would feel much lighter. Mercury pulls just the same!

questions.q: Which of these planets is NOT a giant made of gas or ice?
questions.explain: Mars is a small rocky planet; Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants, Neptune an ice giant.

questions.q: Which planet is about five times farther from the Sun than Earth is?
questions.explain: Jupiter is about 5.2 times as far from the Sun as Earth is.

questions.q: Which planet is about thirty times farther from the Sun than Earth is?
questions.explain: Neptune is about 30 times as far from the Sun as Earth, which is why it is so cold.

questions.q: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.explain: Light is very fast, but the Sun is very far away, so its light takes about 8 minutes to get here.

questions.q: Which planet has two small moons called Phobos and Deimos?
questions.explain: Phobos and Deimos are small, lumpy moons that go around Mars.

questions.q: Which planet is wrapped in thick clouds of acid?
questions.explain: Venus has thick clouds of acid, and its air traps heat, which makes it the hottest planet.

questions.q: Which planet is the closest to the Sun, but is not the hottest?
questions.explain: Venus is hotter than Mercury because its thick air traps the heat.

questions.q: Which planet takes about 165 Earth years to go once around the Sun?
questions.explain: Neptune is so far away that one of its years lasts about 165 Earth years.

questions.q: About how many Earth years does Jupiter take to go once around the Sun?
questions.explain: Jupiter's year is about 12 Earth years long.

questions.q: How long is a year on Mars?
questions.explain: Mars is farther from the Sun than Earth, so its trip around the Sun takes 687 days, nearly two Earth years.

questions.q: How many of the eight planets are giants made of gas or ice?
questions.explain: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune are the four giants. The other four are rocky.

questions.q: Which planet has a big moon called Titan, with thick air of its own?
questions.explain: Titan is Saturn's biggest moon, and it is the only moon with a thick atmosphere.

questions.q: Which planet has an icy moon called Europa that may hide an ocean under its ice?
questions.explain: Europa is one of Jupiter's moons. Scientists think a deep ocean of water lies under its icy crust.
